newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-TYSON ABANDONS TOLSTOY FOR THE COMICS.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TYSON ABANDONS TOLSTOY FOR THE COMICS.

text.p: It's simple, really, for Mike Tyson now: why read Tolstoy when you have comic books?

When the former undisputed heavyweight champion of the world was in prison, much was made of his claim that he was holed up in his cell reading the classics, including Tolstoy, Voltaire and Mark Twain.

Tyson became so enamoured of the life of Mao Zedong he even had a likeness of the late Chinese leader tattooed on his right arm. All of this hinted that Tyson, the former street thug, the man who once boasted of trying to punch nose bones into the brains of his opponents, was really an intellectual diamond in the rough, discovering the joys of the contemplative life.

But since his release from an Indiana State prison in March, 1995, after three years on a rape conviction, Tyson, who over the years has revealed an often perceptive and inquisitive mind, obviously has eased demands on his intellect.
Tyson, who will fight World Boxing Association champion Bruce Seldon on Saturday, was asked in an impromptu interview with reporters earlier this week what he reads these days.

"I read the Marvel (comic books). That stuff. When I was in prison I was wrapped up in all those deep books. That Tolstoy crap. People shouldn't read that stuff," Tyson said. "When we read these books what purpose does it serve in this day and time? What purpose does it serve?"

While the classics don't seem to weigh on Tyson's mind much now, his three years in prison and especially the terms of his three years of parole, which forbids travel without the court's permission, apparently do.
Tyson, jailed for raping a beauty contestant in Indianapolis, was asked about fighting outside the United States.
"I have no freedom. I'm a free man on stipulations," he said, referring to the terms of his parole.
"I'm a convicted felon. I can't go anywhere. Shoot, they think I'm Al Capone, man," said Tyson, referring to an infamous U.S. gangster of years ago. "Where am I going to go?"

Moving from subject to subject in almost a stream of consciousness, Tyson talked about his 220-pound (98 kg), declawed, pet tiger, Kenya, and about how he has to be careful around her because she plays roughly and nearly knocked him out once when she jumped on him.
Stating the obvious, Tyson said, "I'm not diplomatic. I don't know if that's a bad thing or a good thing. Maybe I'm not refined enough or maybe I'm just too stupid.
"The fact is I always admired those guys, the rebellious people," he said. "I don't want to be arrogant," he said, but "I'd rather suffer than tolerate bullshit."
